_why: Skill-candidates row '`--check-anchors` should sweep every spec directory by default': a habitual one-directory sweep said ANCHORS_OK while `h-mad/tests/specs/` had drifted. A no-argument `--check-anchors` now discovers every committed spec through `git ls-files` and the classifier. These rows prove the tests bite if discovery narrows back to one directory, admits untracked files, or turns a failed discovery into an empty (vacuous) sweep.

mutations.name: discovery-narrows-to-one-directory
mutations._mechanism: The defect the row records, restored: only `mutation-specs/` is swept and a drifted `specs/` spec is invisible.
mutations.find: paths = sorted(repo / rel for rel in listed.stdout.split("\0") if rel)
mutations.replace: paths = sorted(repo / rel for rel in listed.stdout.split("\0") if rel and "/mutation-specs/" in "/" + rel)

mutations.name: discovery-failure-becomes-an-empty-sweep
mutations._mechanism: Fail-open: git cannot answer, the sweep gets [] and reports NOTHING_SWEPT instead of saying discovery failed.
mutations.find:
if top.returncode != 0:
        raise SpecError(f"could not discover committed specs: {top.stderr.strip()}")

mutations.name: discovery-walks-the-filesystem-not-the-index
mutations._mechanism: An untracked scratch spec joins the sweep, so a committed-only property reads someone's local file.
mutations.find: paths = sorted(repo / rel for rel in listed.stdout.split("\0") if rel)

mutations.name: non-specs-are-swept-as-noise
mutations._mechanism: Every tracked JSON prints a SKIPPED line, burying the findings the sweep exists to show.
mutations.find: return [p for p in paths if classify_spec_file(p)[0] != "not-a-spec"]
